title: Affine shrinking downstairs under a finite radicial morphism
statement: Let $g:V\to S$ be a finite universally injective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-radicial-morphism], $x\in V$ and $O\subset V$ an open neighbourhood of $x$. There is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subset S$ of $g(x)$ such that $g^{-1}(U)\subset O$. Neither surjectivity of $g$ nor affineness or reducedness of $S$ is required.

proof.text: The image g(V minus O) is closed because g is finite. It misses g(x), because injectivity forces every point over g(x) to equal x. Its complement is thus an open neighbourhood of g(x).

Choose an affine open neighbourhood U of g(x) inside this complement. If y maps into U, then y cannot lie outside O, since otherwise g(y) would lie in the excluded image. This is the desired inverse-image containment.
